svg.text: Trials that stop early are reported more often than trials that finish
anyone assuming unreported trials are the failed ones
where in the register the missing results actually are
terminated trials report less than completed ones, inside the
share reporting results within three years, with 95% intervals
completions 2012–2021, so every cell has three years of follow-up
A terminated trial is the one nobody wants to write up — the drug did not work, the money
went, the enrolment never came. If the register's silence had a shape, that is where it
should be deepest. It is the other way round, and the effect is largest inside the
university and hospital group, which is about 70% of both arms and has the lowest reporting
A mechanism. Stopping early may close a
project in a way finishing does not, but
the register cannot separate that from a
dozen other stories. The measured fact is
the ratio. Withdrawn studies are excluded:
they never enrolled anyone, so there is
ClinicalTrials.gov API v2, fetched 2026-09-22. Population as figure 3, restricted to completions 2012–2021. Intervals are 95% Wilson, drawn because
the cells span two orders of magnitude — the two classes that reverse the finding have 133 and 147 terminated trials and their intervals say so.
Classes with under 120 completed or 100 terminated trials are not drawn.
